analysis_notes.summary: Torah #113 describes the experience of someone for whom Hashem's presence glimmers (מִתְנוֹצֵץ): even performing a single act not in complete holiness causes deep regret and shame (חֲרָטָה, בּוּשָׁה). The key concepts — הִתְנוֹצְצוּת הַשֵּׁם (God's glimmering), שְׁלֵמוּת הַקְּדֻשָּׁה (completeness of holiness), חֲרָטָה (regret), בּוּשָׁה (shame), נֶפֶשׁ (soul) — are presented in a causal/conditional framework (if X happens, Y follows), not as parallel aspects of the same essence. No bechina language appears in the text. No packages can be formed.
